summary: Everyone except citizens of India needs a Bhutan visa, applied for online (US$40) directly or through a licensed tour operator (Bangladeshi and Maldivian citizens can also get theirs on arrival), and visitors pay the Sustainable Development Fee — US$100 per person per night for most foreigners. Indian nationals instead obtain an entry permit and pay a lower daily fee.

fee.notes: One-off visa application fee paid online. The Sustainable Development Fee is charged separately for the full stay: US$100 per person per night until 31 August 2027 — half the standard US$200, under an incentive the Department of Immigration states — with US$50 for children aged 6–12 and nothing under 6.

currencyLimits.text: Bhutan's Department of Tourism says you may bring cash equivalent to US$10,000 into the country. The UK Foreign Office says foreign currency worth US$10,000 or more taken into or out of Bhutan must be declared and cleared with the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan.

notes: You can bring a small supply of tobacco for personal use, but the UK government says you must pay taxes and duties on it and be able to show proof of payment if asked; Canada's travel advice puts the tax at 200% and says smoking is prohibited in public places.
It is illegal to take antiques out of Bhutan, and customs officials may inspect items that look like antiques (UK government).

safety.text: Australia advises normal safety precautions in Bhutan. The crime rate is low and violent crime is rare, though petty crime such as theft, pickpocketing and bag snatching can happen. Altitude sickness is a risk above 2,500 m, and flooding and landslides can disrupt transport in the June–September monsoon.

tips.text: Budget for the Sustainable Development Fee: US$100 per person per night for most visitors until 31 August 2027 (half the standard US$200; US$50 for children 6–12, free under 6), paid together with the visa application. Indian nationals pay Nu. 1,200 (or the equivalent in Indian rupees) per night instead.
The UK government says you need to use tour guides when visiting places of interest, or you may be refused entry, and that permits are needed for some areas — your guide can arrange them.

Australia's Smartraveller says altitude sickness is a risk above 2,500 m and that your travel insurance should cover medical evacuation from altitude; Canada notes that several trekking trails exceed 5,000 m.
Dress respectfully when visiting temples and dzongs (UK government), and ask your guide before taking pictures or filming inside dzongs, temples and monasteries (Canada).

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold an Indian passport (Indian nationals need an entry permit instead). Bangladeshi and Maldivian citizens can get the visa on arrival, though the Department of Tourism recommends arranging it beforehand. Everyone else applies online at immi.gov.bt — directly or through a tour operator — paying a US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee, before travel. A tourist may stay for the actual duration of the trip, up to 90 days.

faq.question: How much is Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee?
faq.answer: US$100 per person per night for most foreign visitors, with discounts for children (US$50 for ages 6–12, free under 6). Bhutan's Department of Immigration says this is a 50% reduction of the standard US$200 rate, valid until 31 August 2027. Indian nationals pay ₹1,200 per night. The fee funds healthcare, education and conservation, and is paid before your visa or permit is issued.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: No visa, but they need an entry permit — applied for online before travel or at the port of entry, using a passport or voter identity card — and they pay the Sustainable Development Fee of Nu. 1,200 (or the equivalent in Indian rupees) per night.

faq.question: Do I have to book a tour to visit Bhutan?
faq.answer: You can apply for the visa yourself at immi.gov.bt, and Bhutan's Department of Tourism says the whole journey can be booked independently, but that it is mandatory to be accompanied by a guide at all times. The UK government says you need to use tour guides when visiting places of interest, or you may be refused entry, and Canada's travel advice says you must buy a travel package from an authorised travel agent.

faq.question: How do I apply for a Bhutan visa?
faq.answer: Apply online at immi.gov.bt and pay the US$40 visa fee together with the Sustainable Development Fee. Bhutan's Department of Tourism says a correctly completed application can take up to five days to process.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes, if you apply before your visa or permit expires. Bhutan's Department of Tourism says extensions are applied for through the online visa portal, where the extension fee and the Sustainable Development Fee for the extra nights are paid.
